name: Kim Jong-il
role: Supreme Leader of North Korea (1994–2011); General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea (1997–2011); chairman of the National Defence Commission (1993–2011)
summary: Kim Jong-il led North Korea's one-party state in the name of the Juche idea, a socialism centred on a supreme leader, the party and national self-reliance. He defended state ownership, central planning and party control of ideology and media, rejected market economy and multi-party democracy, and made the military the centre of state policy (Songun). He pursued independent reunification of Korea, opposed foreign troops and 'globalization', and built a nuclear deterrent.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Described the free medical care guaranteed to everyone from birth as a core advantage of socialism and ordered its improvement in 2011.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Condemned the capitalist market economy and warned that introducing it destroys socialism.

public-ownership.rationale: Defended socialist ownership by the state and all the people, with cooperative ownership beside it, as the base of socialism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Held that private ownership breeds individualism and bourgeois ideas and must not replace socialist ownership.

cut-welfare.rationale: Praised free medical care, free education, rent-free housing and abolished taxes as marks of socialism; cutting such programs runs against his stated policy.

strong-leader.rationale: Said the masses become an independent driving force only under a preeminent leader and demanded absolute loyalty to the leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Rejected the withering away of the state, saying socialist power will never wither away.

empower-police-military.rationale: Made military-first (Songun) politics the guiding line and put the army at the centre of state and society.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Called for keeping alive national cultural heritage, customs and traditions and rejected national nihilism.

free-trade.rationale: Rejected 'globalization' and 'integration' as imperialist schemes and warned that careless economic exchange invites imperialist influence.

nation-first.rationale: Promoted a Korean-nation-first principle while saying nationalism and internationalism do not conflict.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Described foreign intervention and 'globalization' as imperialist domination, not as protection of rights.

revolution-justified.rationale: Described the Korean revolution and the struggle against imperialism, including armed struggle, as justified and supported revolutionary change.

central-planning.rationale: Wrote that the socialist economy is a planned, unified economy and rejected the claim that planning lowers productivity.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Held that the party and state must give unified guidance to the economy and give priority to leading sectors such as power industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wanted means of production in state and cooperative hands, and saw private ownership as the base for exploiters, not as something to spread.

one-party-rule.rationale: Argued that the working-class party must be the guiding force of socialist society and rejected a multi-party system as bourgeois.

democracy-best.rationale: Dismissed liberal democracy as a false, bourgeois form and presented socialist democracy under party leadership as the genuine one.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said the people should be armed and ready for a bloody struggle if attacked, and praised the anti-Japanese armed struggle.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Described the Korean nation as homogeneous in blood and language and as a single people.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Held that the masses' struggle for independence, not class struggle alone, drives history, departing from historical materialism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said socialism is not a society where everyone has an equal share but one where people are rewarded according to their work.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Demanded that Japan make a sincere apology and due compensation for its colonial rule over Korea.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Condemned individualism, selfishness and the cult of money as bourgeois ideology.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Held that in socialist society collective interests set the standard and individuals should subordinate their interests to the collective.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Insisted ideological work comes first and that policy must follow socialist ideology.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Described capitalism as treating workers as producers of surplus value to be exploited and used unemployment to lower labour costs.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Endorsed the dictatorship of the people's government over hostile forces and said the socialist state is needed.

collective-farming.rationale: Ran and praised cooperative farming and directed cooperative farms to solve their own supply problems.

total-state.rationale: Held that the party and state must guide the economy, education, media and culture in a unified way.

national-self-determination.rationale: Held that every nation has the right to independence and that the present era is one of independence.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Rejected national nihilism and told artists to inherit and develop national traditions.

dominated-front.rationale: Called on socialist, non-aligned and developing countries to unite under independence against imperialist domination.

workers-nation.rationale: Said nationalism is a prerequisite for internationalism and that revolutionaries must serve their own nation first.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said state power in exploitative societies is a weapon for ruling over the masses, while holding that socialist state power serves the masses.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Held socialism could be built and defended in one country; said success in one's own country is the national duty to the world revolution.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Argued the socialist state's functions intensify against imperialist pressure and that it is needed even in communist society.

vanguard-party.rationale: Held that the working class needs its party and leader to be guided and wrote theory of party building on the leadership role of the party.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said the party must supervise media, art and literature and the education system so that they serve party ideology.

party-commands-army.rationale: Wrote that the People's Army can exist and act only under the leadership of the Party and the leader.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Required a monolithic ideological system, strong organization and discipline in the party.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Made independent, peaceful reunification of the divided homogeneous nation the nation's main task.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Said sovereignty required its own nuclear deterrent in the face of the US nuclear threat.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Backed a Democratic Federal Republic of Koryo of one nation, one state, two systems and two governments.

leader-cult.rationale: Wrote and directed a monolithic ideological system centred on the leader, with statues, portraits and mass praise of Kim Il Sung.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Said applying the material world's laws mechanically to society gives a one-sided view and that the masses and their consciousness drive history.

moral-incentives.rationale: Set political and moral incentives as the main stress, combined with material incentives, and criticized relying only on material ones.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Treated colonial rule as obliteration of nations and as aggression, not as benefit.

patriotic-education.rationale: Told schools and the party to build pride in the nation and the Korean-nation-first spirit.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Wrote that capitalism is sinking toward bankruptcy and that its reforms are only a farce to escape crisis.

party-own-road.rationale: Said each revolutionary party must follow independence and not be directed or interfered with by others.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Made self-reliance a guiding principle of socialist construction, though the state also accepted foreign aid in practice.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Called fascism's 'national socialism' reactionary totalitarianism but rejected labelling socialism totalitarian.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Gave the army a leading role in defending socialism and state affairs under Songun, though under party command.

corporate-influence.rationale: Wrote that monopoly capitalists manipulate politics and that states and parties act on their will.

non-intervention.rationale: Condemned interference by great powers and by other parties in the affairs of independent countries.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Attacked worshipping big powers and dependence on foreign forces as the road to national ruin.

defeat-communism.rationale: Held that socialism must defeat imperialism and that communism should not be abandoned for coexistence with capitalist restoration.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: wrote that only a nation that keeps the purity of its own language can develop independently.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejected any third course between socialism and capitalism, including the mixed economy and social democracy.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Rejected pluralism and a multi-party system, and called the people's government's dictatorship over hostile elements a defence of human rights.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned imperialist exploitation of dependent and colonial countries.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Built a large army and said that armed strength is essential to defend the country.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Wrote that the party should hold up a loyal heir to the leader; he himself succeeded his father and brought his son Kim Jong Un into the line of succession.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Wrote that in capitalist society the mass media and education are in monopoly capitalists' hands so progressive ideas cannot develop freely.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Defended the dictatorship function of the people's government against hostile elements.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Demanded the withdrawal of US troops from south Korea as an obstacle to reunification.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Supported distribution according to work done and denounced the exploitation of labour by property owners.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Described the nation as having a time-honoured history of thousands of years and a continuing culture.

independent-unions.rationale: Placed working people's organizations under party leadership and supervision, not independent of it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Said working people must be masters of the state and society, led by the working-class party.

free-public-college.rationale: Cited free education, with no tuition fees, as an achievement of the socialist system.

public-service-media.rationale: Said media must be supervised by the party as ideological tools, not independent of government.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Stated in 2011 that the DPRK acquired a nuclear deterrent because of the US threat and presided over tests in 2006 and 2009.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Called 'glasnost' and 'pluralism' counterrevolutionary and said multi-party competition only embellishes bourgeois democracy.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Called for defending socialist ownership and the planned economy against capitalist restoration and imperialist pressure.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Wrote that communism and nationalism both express love of country and people and that true communists must be patriots.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Said abandoning party and state guidance of the economy and bringing in a capitalist market economy was the error of socialism's renegades.

notes: Works published under his name count as his words, whoever drafted them. Late works (2011 public health talk, ITAR-Tass interview) show a continued line on Songun, the nuclear deterrent and free medical care. The record includes political repression, a 1990s famine and unfree press, per the Wikipedia reference; none of that is in his own texts and is not used to answer statements without his stated position.
